name: bed_in_the_square
caption: why is there a BED in our village square 🛏️
logline: A boy guards the bed his grandma has kept in the middle of the village for forty years, the day his dad comes to take it down, and finds out what it was for.
question: why tf is there a bed in the middle of the village?
premise: A single red bed has stood in the middle of the village square for forty years. Nobody may sleep in it or build around it; when the village paved the square they moved the well instead. Grandma makes it every morning. Grandpa Walt walked east forty years ago to see where the world ends. Dad says she's waiting for a dead man and plans to take the bed down for the market.
twist: The bed is Grandpa's respawn point. He never slept anywhere else, so the only way home from the far side of the world was to die. At dawn the chat says 'Walt left the confines of this world' (the world border's death message): he reached the edge, and the edge sent him home. He appears beside the bed. Grandma: 'You're late.'

N.name: me (Finn)
N.profile: a teenage boy telling a friend about his grandma; hushed, fond, a little embarrassed for her at first; steadier and braver by the end
N.on_screen: player actor (recording bot, skin noor), seen in camera shots from behind or the side; POV for one shot

Grandma.name: Grandma Ada
Grandma.profile: old, dry and completely certain; never raises her voice; a smile under every line, even the stern ones
Grandma.on_screen: player actor 'Ada', skin alex (the second default skin: the original couple)

Dad.name: Dad (Hal)
Dad.profile: tired, practical, loves his mother and has given up hoping; gentle, not cruel; breaks once
Dad.on_screen: player actor 'Hal', skin kai, an iron axe from L08 on

Walt.name: Grandpa Walt
Walt.on_screen: player actor 'Walt', skin steve (the first default skin), empty-handed and unarmored (he dropped everything at the border); seen only in S13-S14

requests.direction: A village at dawn. A teenage boy tells a friend about his grandmother and the bed she keeps in the square; the grandmother is old, dry and sure of herself.
A tired, gentle man in his forties talks to his elderly mother in a village square.

lines.text: There's a BED / in the middle / of my village. / It's been there / FORTY YEARS.
lines.say: There's a bed in the middle of my village. <short pause> It's been there... forty years.
lines.direction: hushed, like sharing a family secret; a held breath before the number

lines.text: Nobody's allowed / to SLEEP in it. / When they built / the square, / they moved / the WELL / instead.
lines.direction: dry and amused; a tiny beat before the last word

lines.text: Grandma makes it / every MORNING. / Like he's / coming home / TONIGHT.
lines.direction: fond, a little embarrassed for her

lines.text: Keep it CLEAR. / If it's BLOCKED, / he wakes up / somewhere ELSE.
lines.say: Keep it clear. <short pause> If it's blocked, he wakes up somewhere else.
lines.direction: stern but unhurried, shooing someone away; certain, as if stating the weather

lines.text: Grandpa WALT / walked EAST / forty years ago / to see where / the world ENDS.
lines.direction: storytelling, a little wonder; slow down on the last three words

lines.text: He never slept / in another bed. / Not ONCE.
lines.say: He never slept in another bed. <short pause> Not once.
lines.direction: quiet pride, private, almost to herself

lines.text: There IS / no end, / Ma. / He's GONE.
lines.say: There is no end, Ma. <short pause> He's gone.
lines.direction: gentle and worn out, a speech he has made many times

lines.text: The village wants / the square / for the MARKET. / Dad said / he'd take / the bed / at DAWN.
lines.direction: flat dread creeping in; the last word lands heavy

lines.text: So I sat up / with Grandma. / ALL night.
lines.say: So I sat up with Grandma. <short pause> All night.

lines.text: At DAWN, / Dad came / with the AXE. / I stood / in his WAY.
lines.say: At dawn, Dad came with the axe. <short pause> I stood in his way.
lines.direction: tense, quick; the second sentence slower and braver
his voice catches on the second word; very soft
dry as ever, trembling underneath, a smile you can hear

beats_without_lines.what: Silence. The chat line appears bottom-left: 'Walt left the confines of this world' (vanilla death.attack.outsideBorder). Dad stops mid-step. Also drawn in the caption track, white, two chunks.
Grandma stands, smooths the blanket, steps back. Walt appears beside the bed (vanilla respawn: standing, empty-handed), his name 'Walt' above his head. Hold ~1.3 s before L12.
